content.overview: Section 129A lets the Central Government require a prescribed class of unlisted companies to prepare financial results periodically, in the form, manner and at the intervals prescribed, and to obtain approval of the board and complete audit or limited review as prescribed.
content.glance: Section 129A empowers the Central Government to require prescribed classes of unlisted companies to prepare periodical financial results, in the form and at the intervals prescribed.
content.study:
## Statutory rule
Section 129A provides that the Central Government may require such class or classes of unlisted companies, as may be prescribed, to prepare the financial results of the company on a periodical basis, in such form and manner and for such period as may be prescribed, to obtain approval of the board of directors, and to complete audit or limited review of such results in such manner as may be prescribed.

A copy is filed with the Registrar within thirty days of completion of the relevant period.

## Answer structure
The section is for a prescribed class of unlisted companies. It does not by itself name every unlisted company. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: The section was inserted by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2020. It does not apply until a class is prescribed. It is not a substitute for the annual financial statements under section 129.
